subtype: Approach: working backward from the fair date [Thinking]
passage: Maria pressed her thumb on the calendar in the hall. The science fair was on the twenty-fourth, exactly three weeks away. "Last week is for the display board," she muttered, and drew a box round the final seven days. "Middle week is the experiment. So the first week is..." She counted backwards with her pencil, stopped at a Monday and tapped it. "Start here. Not later." Her friend Shreya leaned over from the sofa. "You haven't even picked what to grow yet." "That's the Monday job," Maria said, and wrote CHOOSE PLANT in the first box. Her shoulders felt a little lighter.

qa.q: How many weeks were there until the science fair?
qa.a: There were three weeks until the science fair.

qa.q: What was Maria feeling as she wrote CHOOSE PLANT in the first box?
qa.a: A little relieved, because the plan gave her a clear place to begin; the passage says her shoulders felt lighter.

qa.q: What other approach could Maria use if she is unsure the experiment fits in one week, and why?
qa.a: She could list each step of the experiment and guess how long each takes, so the middle week is based on real needs rather than a round number.

qa.q: How might Shreya see Maria's plan?
qa.a: Shreya seems to find it early, since no plant is chosen yet, but Maria has already given that a slot on the first Monday. 🙂

grounding: A girl plans a science fair project by fixing the end date first and placing each stage before it.

"Sudha Masi, the science fair is on the twenty-first. That's three weeks."
"Plenty of time, then."
"No, listen. Start from the end. What do I need on the last day?"
"Your board, I suppose."
"Right. The display board takes a whole week, with the chart and photos. So week three is the board."
"And before that?"
"The plants need time to grow. That's week two, the experiment."
"Then week one?"
"Buying pots and seeds and setting up. So I start this Saturday, not next month."
Sudha laughed. "You planned it backwards."
"It's the only way I knew when to start."
Sunaina drew three boxes on the calendar and wrote BOARD in the last one in her neatest letters.

qa.q: How did Sunaina feel when Sudha said there was plenty of time?

qa.q: What else could Sunaina add to her plan, and why?
qa.a: She could leave a few spare days before the board week, because plants or photos might take longer than expected.

qa.q: How does the backwards plan look to Sudha?
qa.a: Sudha is amused and impressed, laughing that Sunaina planned it backwards.

passage:
When our teacher said the science fair was in three weeks, I felt a jolt. I remembered last year, when I was still gluing my chart at midnight. So this time I started from the fair and walked backwards. The last week had to be for the display board, because making it neat always takes me forever. The week before that was for the experiment: melting ice cubes in different cups and timing them. That meant the first week was for getting cups, a thermometer and a stopwatch from school. When I finished, Ammi read my three-box plan and said, "My clever girl." I stuck it above my desk, and I started collecting cups the very next day. My name was first on the list.
- Zeenat

qa.a: Zeenat's experiment was melting ice cubes in different cups and timing them.

qa.q: How did Zeenat feel when the teacher announced the fair?
qa.a: Zeenat felt a jolt of worry, remembering gluing the chart at midnight last year.

qa.q: What else could Zeenat do if the experiment week runs late?
qa.a: Zeenat could start the board's title and layout early, so the last week has less to do.

qa.q: How does the plan look to Ammi?
qa.a: Ammi is proud and pleased, calling Zeenat a clever girl after reading the plan.
